newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan tea prices fall on poor quality.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan tea prices fall on poor quality.

text.p: Tea prices fell virtually across the board at the Colombo auction mainly because of poor quality, brokers said on Wednesday.
"The bulk of the teas fell in value mainly due to inferior quality," said a broker at Forbes and Walker.

Some buyers were also not as active as usual, fearing that the possibility of curfews to quell violence after Friday's local government poll could hold up the disposal of tea and force them to incur high financing costs, he said.
Brokers said the current Western quality season had failed to produce good teas because of bad weather.
"The traditional Western quality was not achieved because of bad weather," the Forbes broker said. "We had heavy rains, drought. We also need very cold nights, which we did not have."
The anticipated gross auction average price for the 5.8 million kg on offer fell to 103.10 rupees ($1.79) per kg from 103.29 rupees last week, Forbes and Walker said.
The Commonwealth of Independent States, the biggest buyer of Ceylon tea, was active but selective, brokers said.
The next auction is on March 25-26 where 4.8 million kg will be on offer. ($1=57.64 rupees)
